presentation.text: Meet Minutrel. Open-source time tracking, by project.
Track the work. Capture the context. See where your time goes.
Turn your month into clear, shareable reports.
Work solo on your computer. Or together, on your own server.
Your projects. Your time. Your data. Minutrel.

tutorial.text: Minutrel tracks work by project. Use it on your own computer, or with a team on your own server. Let’s record a session.
Projects give every session a home. We’ll use Atlas for this walkthrough.
In Overview, select your project. You can also choose a task if you need one.
Give the session a short description, so you can recognise the work later.
Click Start. Minutrel now tracks your time against Atlas while you work.
Taking a break? Click Pause. This time won’t count as work.
Click Resume to continue the same session, with the same project and description.
When you’re done, click Finish to save the session. Closing the window doesn’t stop the timer.
Open Time entries to see your completed sessions for the month you’ve selected.
Forgot to start the timer? Add time manually. Choose a project and date, enter forty-five minutes, and describe the work.
Save the entry. It’s now included in your totals.
Time shows how much. Your work journal explains what moved forward.
Add a note for Atlas. Capture a result, a decision, or the next step, while it’s still fresh.
Notes are private by default. Tick this box to share the note in team reports, then save it.
Reports bring completed time and shared work together. See where the month went, by project and by person.
Choose the month you need. An administrator can filter the team and download a report.
Export a PDF, a CSV, or a ZIP package. Here, we’ll download a PDF.
Choose a project. Track your time. Add context. Review the results. That’s Minutrel.
